title: G7 Lean System
description: Overview of G7 Lean System and its supported features.
markdown:
# Overview and requirements

G7 Lean System adds an in-game interface for preparing fictional roleplay drinks. Recipe state is stored on inventory items as metadata, so a measured bottle can retain its syrup type and remaining lines, and a finished drink can retain its recipe, potency, ice state, and remaining sips.

## Features in the package

- G7-branded NUI interface.
- Five syrup profiles and two soda profiles.
- Measured syrup bottles and soda-filled cups.
- Four potency tiers: Light, Medium, Strong, and Heavy.
- Ice state and per-drink sip tracking.
- Configurable screen, camera, movement, ragdoll/blackout, and optional armor effects.
- Configurable prop models, animation dictionaries, and animation clips.
- Framework and inventory bridge code.
- Included inventory item examples and PNG inventory icons.

## Requirements

- A FiveM server running GTA V.
- `ox_lib` started before this resource.
- A supported framework integration: QBCore, Qbox, or ESX.
- A supported inventory: ox_inventory, qb-inventory, a compatible qs-inventory build, or a custom adapter.
- All G7 items registered in the active inventory.

The bridge has a fallback detection value named `standalone`, but the supplied resource does not implement a complete standalone inventory/framework. Treat QBCore, Qbox, and ESX as the framework options unless you build and test your own integration.

## Resource layout

```text
g7_leansystem/
├── client/main.lua
├── server/bridge.lua
├── server/main.lua
├── shared/items.lua
├── config.lua
├── fxmanifest.lua
├── install/inventory/
│   ├── items.lua
│   ├── qb-items.lua
│   └── images/
└── web/
    ├── index.html
    ├── style.css
    ├── app.js
    └── assets/g7-logo.png
```

The `stream/animations/` and `stream/props/` directories are asset locations; the package uses configurable base-game fallback props/animations and does not include custom `.ycd`, `.ydr`, or `.ytyp` assets.

markdown:
# G7 Lean System — Installation

## Requirements

- `ox_lib`
- One framework: QBCore, Qbox or ESX
- One inventory: ox_inventory, qb-inventory, qs-inventory, or a custom adapter
- `ox_target` or `qb-target` (optional, only needed for the target option on placed cups)
- `g7_advanced_progressbar` (optional, any supported progress bar also works)

## Steps

1. Copy the `g7_leansystem` folder into your server's `resources` folder. Keep the folder name exactly `g7_leansystem`.
2. Add the items to your inventory (see the section for your inventory below).
3. Copy every PNG from `install/inventory/images/` into your inventory's item image folder.
4. Add the resource to `server.cfg`, after its dependencies and your inventory:

   ```cfg
   ensure ox_lib
   ensure qb-core            # or qbx_core / es_extended
   ensure ox_inventory       # or qb-inventory / qs-inventory
   ensure g7_leansystem
   ```

5. Restart the server and check the console. You should see the detected framework and inventory.
6. In game, use any G7 lean item, or press `F7` / type `/leanmenu`, to open the mixing lab.

## ox_inventory

1. Merge the entries from `install/inventory/items.lua` into `ox_inventory/data/items.lua`. Do not replace the whole file.
2. Copy the PNGs to `ox_inventory/web/images/`.
3. Keep `consume = 0` and the `export = 'g7_leansystem.useItem'` line on every G7 item.
4. Keep `g7_lean_bottle_filled`, `g7_lean_cup_soda` and `g7_lean_drink` non-stackable (`stack = false`).
5. Restart `ox_inventory`, then `g7_leansystem`.

## qb-inventory / Qbox

1. Merge the entries from `install/inventory/qb-items.lua` into `qb-core/shared/items.lua` (or your Qbox shared items file). Do not replace the whole table.
2. Copy the PNGs to your inventory's image folder (for example `qb-inventory/html/images/`).
3. Keep `unique = true` on `g7_lean_bottle_filled`, `g7_lean_cup_soda` and `g7_lean_drink`.
4. Restart the server.

## qs-inventory

Start with `install/inventory/qb-items.lua` and the same PNGs. If your qs-inventory version does not support the same add / remove / use-item exports, set `Config.Inventory = 'custom'` and fill in the functions below.

## Custom inventory

In `config.lua` set `Config.Inventory = 'custom'` and fill in `Config.CustomInventory`:

```lua
Config.CustomInventory = {
    count = function(source, item) end,                  -- return the item count
    remove = function(source, item, count, metadata) end, -- return true on success
    add = function(source, item, count, metadata) end,    -- keep metadata, return true on success
    registerUse = function(item, callback) end            -- callback(source, itemData)
}
```

## Config choices

Set these in `config.lua` if auto-detection is not right for your server:

```lua
Config.Framework = 'auto'   -- auto, qb, qbox, esx
Config.Inventory = 'auto'   -- auto, ox, qb, qs, custom
Config.Locale    = 'en'     -- en, fr, es
Config.ProgressBar.Provider = 'auto' -- auto, g7, qb, qbox, esx, ox_lib, custom
Config.Interaction.Target = 'auto'   -- auto, ox_target, qb-target, custom, none
Config.Interaction.Text3D = 'auto'   -- auto, always, never
```

If you run more than one inventory resource, set `Config.Inventory` to the one players actually use.

## Shops

Shops are built in game with `/leanadmin` (no file editing). Give your admins access in `server.cfg`:

```
add_ace group.admin g7lean.admin allow
```

(Framework groups and identifiers can also be listed in `Config.Admin`.)

1. Run `/leanadmin` and press **New shop**.
2. Name it, pick cash / bank / both, then **Place shopkeeper** (aim and left click) or **Where I stand**.
3. Choose a map icon, colour and size. **Preview** shows it on your minimap.
4. Switch on the items it sells and set each price, then **Save shop**.

Shops save to `data/store.json` and appear for everyone immediately. Back up or move shops by copying that file. The three example shops in `Config.Shop.Locations` are only created the first time the script starts.

Interaction uses ox_target or qb-target when running (`Config.Shop.Target`), otherwise an `E` prompt. Money works with QBCore, Qbox and ESX out of the box. For standalone with ox_inventory, cash is the `money` item (`Config.Shop.CashItem`). For anything else, fill in `Config.CustomMoney`.

title: Lean System — First-time setup
description: Configure framework, inventory, and first-run settings.
markdown:
# First-time setup and gameplay

## Open the mixing interface

Use any registered G7 Lean System item to open the interface, run `/leanmenu`, or press **F7** by default.

## Preparation flow

### Measure syrup

You need one syrup item and one empty baby bottle. Select a syrup and a line amount in the interface. The server validates the syrup key and line count, consumes the ingredients, and creates `g7_lean_bottle_filled` with syrup and line metadata.

The maximum measured bottle amount is controlled by `Config.Security.MaxBottleLines` (default `16`).

### Prepare soda

You need one soda item and one empty cup. Select the soda to create a metadata-bearing `g7_lean_cup_soda`.

### Mix a drink

You need a measured bottle, soda-filled cup, and an additional empty cup. Select a potency tier. The selected tier determines how many lines are used: Light 1, Medium 2, Strong 3, Heavy 4. The soda cup and empty cup are consumed; if the bottle has lines remaining, a new measured bottle is returned. The finished drink records syrup, soda, potency, lines, sips, and ice state.

### Add ice

Use an ice item with a valid finished drink through the interface's Add Ice action. The drink is replaced with an iced version, and the ice is consumed.

### Sip, pass, or discard

When a finished drink is active, the default controls are:

- **E:** take a sip.
- **C:** pass the drink to a nearby player.
- **X:** discard the drink.
- **G:** the current implementation displays a reminder that the drink remains saved in inventory; it does not implement a separate stash action.

The default maximum sip count is `20`, configured by `Config.Security.MaxCupSips`. When the last sip is consumed, the drink item is replaced by an empty cup.

## Persistence

There is no database requirement in the supplied resource. Recipe and sip state is carried in inventory item metadata. This relies on the selected inventory correctly preserving metadata for unique/non-stackable items.

markdown:
# Configuration reference

Edit `config.lua`. Restart the resource after changing settings unless your server's workflow explicitly reloads them.

## Brand and detection

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config.Brand.Name` | `G7 Development` | Brand name used by the resource. |
| `Config.Brand.Product` | `G7 Lean System` | Product name shown in notifications. |
| `Config.Brand.Accent` | `#5b376a` | UI accent color. |
| `Config.Brand.Logo` | `assets/g7-logo.png` | UI logo path. |
| `Config.Debug` | `false` | Debug toggle; current code has limited use of this flag. |
| `Config.Framework` | `auto` | `auto`, `qb`, `qbox`, or `esx`. |
| `Config.Inventory` | `auto` | `auto`, `ox`, `qb`, `qs`, or `custom`. |

Automatic framework detection checks `qbx_core`, then `qb-core`, then `es_extended`. Automatic inventory detection checks `ox_inventory`, then `qs-inventory`, then `qb-inventory`. If multiple resources are running, set the inventory explicitly to the one players actually use.

## Security

| Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `Config.Security.MaxDistance` | `3.0` | Configured maximum distance; review usage in the installed version before relying on it as a universal action limit. |
| `Config.Security.ActionCooldown` | `900` | Server action cooldown in milliseconds. |
| `Config.Security.PassDistance` | `2.5` | Maximum distance for passing a drink. |
| `Config.Security.MaxLinesPerDrink` | `4` | Configured maximum lines per drink; potency tiers currently use 1–4 lines. |
| `Config.Security.MaxBottleLines` | `16` | Maximum lines allowed in a measured bottle. |
| `Config.Security.MaxCupSips` | `20` | Starting sip count for a finished drink. |
| `Config.Security.LogRejectedActions` | `true` | Log rejected/invalid action attempts. |

The server applies a per-player cooldown, validates recipe identifiers and line/potency values, checks ingredients, and checks pass distance. Do not treat configuration values as a substitute for validating third-party inventory behavior.

## Progress durations

All values are milliseconds.

| Setting | Default |
|---|---:|
| `Config.Progress.Pour` | `4500` |
| `Config.Progress.Soda` | `3000` |
| `Config.Progress.Mix` | `5000` |
| `Config.Progress.Ice` | `2500` |
| `Config.Progress.Sip` | `2800` |

## Controls

| Setting | Default control | GTA control ID |
|---|---|---:|
| `Config.Controls.Sip` | E | `38` |
| `Config.Controls.Stow` | G | `47` |
| `Config.Controls.Pass` | C | `26` |
| `Config.Controls.Discard` | X | `73` |

The G/stow control currently displays a notification; it does not move the drink into another inventory location.

## Items, syrups, sodas, and potency

`Config.Items` contains the item IDs used for the empty bottle, measured bottle, empty cup, soda cup, ice, finished drink, and cup stack. Item IDs must match the names registered in the active inventory.

`Config.Syrups` defines five syrup profiles: `violet`, `royal`, `gold`, `crimson`, and `azure`. Each profile contains a display label, UI color, inventory item ID, screen effect, timecycle modifier, camera shake, and blackout multiplier.

`Config.Sodas` defines `citrus` and `orange`, each with a label, item ID, and UI color.

`Config.Potency` defines `light`, `medium`, `strong`, and `heavy`. Defaults consume 1, 2, 3, and 4 lines respectively and provide an effect intensity value. If you add or rename recipes, also review item registration and the UI assumptions in `web/app.js`.

`Config.Text` contains user-facing messages for common missing-item and invalid-action cases.

# Effects, props, and animations

## Effects

`Config.Effects` controls client-side roleplay effects.

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| `Enabled` | `true` | Master switch for drink effects. |
| `Progressive` | `true` | Scales intensity using the sip count. |
| `Blackout` | `true` | Enables chance-based blackout behavior after the configured sip threshold. |
| `BlackoutStartSip` | `8` | Sip count at which blackout checks begin. |
| `BaseBlackoutChance` | `4` | Base chance percentage. |
| `MaxBlackoutChance` | `25` | Maximum chance percentage. |
| `BlackoutDuration` | `9000` | Ragdoll/blackout duration in milliseconds. |
| `RecoveryDuration` | `4000` | Recovery wait in milliseconds. |
| `ArmorEnabled` | `false` | Enables optional armor changes. |
| `ArmorByPotency` | all `0` | Armor amount by potency tier. |
| `Movement` | `true` | Applies a temporary movement-rate change. |
| `Ragdoll` | `true` | Enables ragdoll during blackout behavior. |
| `EffectDuration` | `45000` | Duration before movement/screen effects are reset. |

Effects are client-side roleplay presentation, not authoritative gameplay security. Tune them to match your server's rules and accessibility expectations.

## Props

`Config.Assets` contains `CupModel`, `BottleModel`, `SodaBottleModel`, `EmptyBottleModel`, `IceModel`, and `SyrupModels`. Defaults use base-game models so the resource does not require a custom prop pack.

If you use custom props, install assets you have permission to use and ensure the configured model names exactly match the streamed model names. Test each model in-game.

## Animations

`Config.Assets.Animations` contains:

- `PourDict` / `PourAnim`
- `DrinkDict` / `DrinkAnim`
- `MixDict` / `MixAnim`

The supplied defaults are base-game fallback animation dictionaries/clips. Custom animation assets are not included in this archive. Only add licensed assets and set dictionary/clip names that actually exist in those assets.

## Cleanup

On resource stop, the client clears NUI focus, timecycle modifiers, screen effects, camera shake, and movement-rate override. Test effect cleanup if you change the client code or introduce additional effects.

title: Lean System — Inventory integrations
description: Supported inventory options and integration notes.
markdown:
# Inventory integrations

The inventory bridge lives in `server/bridge.lua`. Set `Config.Inventory` in `config.lua` to the inventory players actually use.

## ox_inventory

Set:

```lua
Config.Inventory = 'ox'
```

Merge the entries from `install/inventory/items.lua` into your existing item definitions using the format expected by your installed ox_inventory version. Do not replace the entire item registry. Copy `install/inventory/images/*.png` into the configured image directory (commonly `ox_inventory/web/images/`).

The bridge uses `Search`, `RemoveItem`, `AddItem`, and `RegisterUsableItem` exports. Verify those APIs against your installed ox_inventory version.

## qb-inventory / Qbox

For QBCore, use `Config.Framework = 'qb'`; for Qbox, use `Config.Framework = 'qbox'`. Set `Config.Inventory = 'qb'` when using the QB-style inventory bridge.

Merge `install/inventory/qb-items.lua` into the appropriate shared item table. Do not replace your entire item file. Copy images to the directory used by your inventory.

The current bridge uses QBCore-style `GetPlayer`, `GetItemByName`, `RemoveItem`, `AddItem`, and `CreateUseableItem` methods. Confirm your Qbox/inventory version exposes compatible methods.

## qs-inventory

Set `Config.Inventory = 'qs'`. The bridge attempts QBCore-compatible player item methods first, then uses `qs-inventory` exports for count/removal/addition as applicable. QS APIs vary by release and configuration; this integration must be verified against the exact installed version. If the API contract differs, use the custom adapter rather than assuming compatibility.

## ESX

Set `Config.Framework = 'esx'` and select the inventory integration appropriate to your server. The supplied bridge uses ESX inventory methods as a fallback for count, removal, addition, and usable-item registration. The item metadata behavior of a plain ESX inventory may not support the unique metadata-bearing recipe items in the same way as ox_inventory/QB-style inventories. Validate metadata persistence before using the resource in production.

## Multiple inventories installed

Automatic detection chooses the first matching inventory in this order: ox_inventory, qs-inventory, qb-inventory, then custom. If more than one is started, explicitly set `Config.Inventory` to prevent detection from selecting the wrong one.

markdown:
# Items and metadata

Register every item ID below in the inventory used by your server. Item IDs are defined in `config.lua` and `shared/items.lua`.

## Item IDs

| Item ID | Default label / use |
|---|---|
| `g7_lean_syrup_violet` | Violet Reserve syrup |
| `g7_lean_syrup_royal` | Royal Purple syrup |
| `g7_lean_syrup_gold` | Golden Drop syrup |
| `g7_lean_syrup_crimson` | Crimson Blend syrup |
| `g7_lean_syrup_azure` | Azure Night syrup |
| `g7_lean_soda_citrus` | Citrus Soda |
| `g7_lean_soda_orange` | Orange Soda |
| `g7_lean_bottle_empty` | Empty Baby Bottle |
| `g7_lean_bottle_filled` | Measured Syrup Bottle |
| `g7_lean_cup_empty` | G7 Foam Cup |
| `g7_lean_cup_soda` | Soda-Filled Cup |
| `g7_lean_ice` | Ice Cubes |
| `g7_lean_drink` | G7 Mixed Drink |
| `g7_lean_cup_stack` | Stack of G7 Foam Cups |

## Items that must be unique

The following items carry per-instance state and must not stack together:

- `g7_lean_bottle_filled`
- `g7_lean_cup_soda`
- `g7_lean_drink`

The provided ox_inventory definitions use `stack = false` for these items. The QB-style definitions use `unique = true`.

## Metadata fields

The server writes a `g7lean = true` marker and recipe fields to metadata.

- **Measured bottle:** `syrup`, `lines`, `label`, `description`.
- **Soda cup:** `soda`, `label`, `description`.
- **Finished drink:** `syrup`, `soda`, `potency`, `lines`, `sips`, `maxSips`, `iced`, `label`, `description`.

Metadata is read differently depending on the inventory. ox_inventory uses slot metadata; QB/Qbox uses `info` or `metadata` on player item data. Some custom inventory builds store it differently and may require adapting `itemMeta()` in `server/main.lua`.

## Images

The package contains PNGs in `install/inventory/images/`. Copy the images into your inventory's item-image folder and keep the filenames matching the definitions. If your inventory expects a different item-image path or naming convention, update that inventory configuration accordingly.

title: Lean System — Custom inventory
description: Connect an inventory that is not built in.
markdown:
# Custom inventory adapter

Use this page when your inventory is not compatible with the supplied `ox`, `qb`, or `qs` bridge paths.

## Select custom mode

```lua
Config.Inventory = 'custom'
```

Implement the adapter functions in `Config.CustomInventory` in `config.lua`, or extend `server/bridge.lua` using your inventory's documented API.

```lua
Config.CustomInventory = {
    count = function(source, item)
        -- Return the player's numeric count for item.
    end,
    remove = function(source, item, count, metadata)
        -- Remove item/count. Return true only when successful.
    end,
    add = function(source, item, count, metadata)
        -- Add item/count with metadata. Return true only when successful.
    end,
    registerUse = function(item, callback)
        -- Register a usable item; invoke callback(source, itemData) on use.
    end
}
```

## Contract requirements

- `count(source, item)` returns a number, or a value convertible to a number.
- `remove(source, item, count, metadata)` returns `true` only after removal succeeds.
- `add(source, item, count, metadata)` returns `true` only after the item was added successfully.
- `add` must preserve supplied metadata.
- `registerUse(item, callback)` must register the usable item and call `callback(source, itemData)` when used.
- Unique/metadata-bearing items must not stack with different metadata.
- Validate item counts and metadata using the inventory's real API; do not trust client-provided state.

## Important implementation note

The current `G7Bridge` wrapper calls the custom functions from `server/bridge.lua`. Simply defining `Config.CustomInventory` is not enough unless each function is implemented and returns the required values. Test failed additions, full inventories, metadata round-trips, disconnects, and concurrent actions. Rollback attempts cannot guarantee recovery if the inventory itself errors or returns inaccurate status.

title: Lean System — Commands & controls
description: Available commands and key controls.
markdown:
# Commands and controls

## Command

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/leanmenu` | Opens the G7 Lean System interface. |

The command is registered client-side and is not ACE-restricted in the supplied version.

## Key mapping

| Key | Default action |
|---|---|
| `F7` | Open interface (`leanmenu` key mapping) |
| `E` | Sip while a drink is active |
| `C` | Pass the drink to the nearest player within range |
| `X` | Discard the active drink |
| `G` | Displays a reminder; it does not currently implement a separate stow/storage action |

The keys are configurable through `Config.Controls`, except the F7 menu binding, which is registered using FiveM's key mapping for `leanmenu`. Players may be able to change the key mapping through FiveM settings.

## Passing drinks

The client finds a nearby player and sends the target server ID. The server checks that the target exists, is not the sender, and is within `Config.Security.PassDistance`. The server then transfers the drink metadata through the selected inventory adapter.

title: Lean System — Events & callbacks
description: Internal events and callback reference.
markdown:
# Events and callbacks

This page documents the event and callback names found in the `g7_leansystem` v1.0.0 source. Events marked internal are implementation details, not a stable third-party API. Do not trigger server action events from untrusted client code; the server validates several fields, but these are still internal resource interfaces.

## Server event

### `g7_lean:server:action` — internal

Client sends an action string and a payload table. Supported action values in the server handler:

| Action | Payload fields used |
|---|---|
| `pourSyrup` | `syrup` (key from `Config.Syrups`), `lines` (integer) |
| `pourSoda` | `soda` (key from `Config.Sodas`) |
| `mix` | `potency` (key from `Config.Potency`) |
| `addIce` | no client recipe fields; server reads drink and ice inventory state |
| `sip` | no client recipe fields; server reads drink inventory state |
| `pass` | `target` (server ID) |
| `discard` | no client recipe fields; server reads drink inventory state |
| `unpackCups` | no additional fields; handler behavior depends on current implementation |

The server enforces a per-player action cooldown and validates recipe identifiers and ingredients. The event is not intended as a public API contract and may change between versions.

## Client events

| Event | Parameters | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `g7_lean:client:open` | `item`, `data` | Opens the NUI for a usable item; shows active-drink controls when the item is a finished drink. |
| `g7_lean:client:empty` | none | Clears active-drink state and notifies the player the drink is finished. |
| `g7_lean:client:drinkState` | `active` (boolean) | Toggles active-drink controls. |
| `g7_lean:client:effects` | `syrupKey`, `potency`, `sipCount`, `iced` | Applies configured client-side roleplay effects after a sip. |

These events are registered by the client resource. Treat them as internal and avoid relying on them across versions unless G7 Development explicitly confirms support.

## ox_lib callback

### `g7_lean:server:summary`

Registered using `lib.callback.register`. The client awaits it to populate the interface. It returns a table containing:

- `syrups`: array of configured syrup keys, labels, item IDs, counts, and colors.
- `sodas`: array of configured soda keys, labels, item IDs, counts, and colors.
- `items`: inventory counts keyed by configured item names, plus convenience keys such as `emptyBottle`, `filledBottle`, `emptyCup`, `sodaCup`, `ice`, and `drink`.

This callback is an internal UI data source, not a documented third-party API guarantee.

## Public exports

No public Lua exports were explicitly declared in the supplied `fxmanifest.lua` or resource source. Do not expect `exports.g7_leansystem:...` methods in version 1.0.0 unless they are added in a future release.

title: Lean System — NUI & actions
description: NUI callbacks and action flow.
markdown:
# NUI callbacks and action flow

The NUI page is declared as `web/index.html` in `fxmanifest.lua`. The browser communicates with the client Lua script through three registered NUI callbacks.

## NUI callbacks

| Callback | Input | Response / behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `close` | No required fields | Closes the UI and returns `{ ok = true }`. |
| `refresh` | No required fields | Requests `g7_lean:server:summary` through ox_lib and returns the summary table. |
| `action` | `action` string and optional `payload` table | Closes the UI, runs the matching progress/animation, then sends the action to the server if progress succeeds. Returns `{ ok = true }` to the browser. |

## Action lifecycle

1. The UI submits an action and payload.
2. The client closes the UI and runs a progress action using the configured duration.
3. For passing, the client identifies a nearby player and fills in `payload.target`.
4. The client triggers the internal server action event.
5. The server checks the cooldown, action values, ingredients, item metadata, and distance where relevant.
6. The server removes/creates items and sends notifications or effect events.

The immediate NUI response `{ ok = true }` confirms the browser callback was received; it does not guarantee the server-side inventory action succeeded. Use in-game notifications and inventory state to confirm the result.

title: Lean System — Troubleshooting
description: Solutions for common installation and runtime issues.
markdown:
# Troubleshooting

## The resource does not start

- Confirm the folder is named `g7_leansystem`.
- Ensure `ox_lib` and the framework/inventory start before the resource.
- Check for Lua syntax errors in the server console.
- Confirm `fxmanifest.lua` is present in the resource root.

## Wrong framework or inventory is detected

Set `Config.Framework` and `Config.Inventory` explicitly. Auto detection checks Qbox before QBCore, and ox_inventory before qs-inventory and qb-inventory. When multiple resources are running, detection may not select the one players actually use.

## Items do not appear or cannot be used

- Confirm all item IDs from `install/inventory/items.lua` or `qb-items.lua` were merged into the active registry.
- Restart the relevant framework/inventory resource or server as required by your inventory.
- Check spelling and case of each item ID.
- Verify the chosen inventory exposes the API used by the bridge.

## Drink state or recipe is lost

Ensure `g7_lean_bottle_filled`, `g7_lean_cup_soda`, and `g7_lean_drink` are unique/non-stackable. Verify the inventory preserves metadata. For custom inventory formats, adapt `itemMeta()` in `server/main.lua` and test a full round-trip: create, move, relog if applicable, then use.

## UI opens but actions fail

- Check the server console for `[G7 Lean System] rejected action` messages.
- Confirm the player has the exact required ingredients.
- Check that the item metadata has not been modified by another resource.
- Verify inventory add/remove calls return success correctly.
- Test with default configuration and no unrelated inventory overrides.

## Inventory-full messages or missing ingredients after an error

The script attempts to restore consumed ingredients when an add operation fails. Rollback is best-effort and cannot guarantee recovery if the inventory API returns incorrect results, throws during an outage, or behaves differently than expected. Reproduce on a staging server and inspect inventory logs before production.

## Effects do not clear or look incorrect

Confirm `Config.Effects.Enabled` is true, test with default effect settings, and verify the resource is not being stopped unexpectedly. The resource clears common screen/camera/movement effects when stopped; custom effects added by modifications may need their own cleanup.

## Props or animations do not play

The included resource uses base-game fallback models and animation dictionaries. If you configure custom assets, confirm the files are installed, streamed, and licensed for use; then verify the model/dictionary/clip names exactly match the asset.

# Known limitations and update checklist

## Known limitations in version 1.0.0

- No public Lua exports are declared.
- Event names and the summary callback are internal implementation details and may change.
- The `G` control currently displays a reminder; it does not implement a dedicated inventory stow action.
- Custom animation/prop assets are not included. The package uses configurable base-game fallback models and animations.
- qs-inventory compatibility depends on the installed version's exports and item format.
- ESX inventory metadata behavior may differ from the unique metadata behavior expected by measured bottles and drinks; test this before release.
- The script has not been validated against every third-party inventory build or every server configuration.
- Rollback after a failed inventory operation is best-effort, not guaranteed.

## Update checklist

1. Back up `config.lua`, item definitions, and any custom adapter changes.
2. Read the release notes for breaking changes.
3. Replace resource files with the new release while preserving approved customizations.
4. Compare the new `config.lua` with your backup; do not blindly overwrite new settings.
5. Check whether item IDs, metadata fields, events, callbacks, or dependencies changed.
6. Restart on a staging server and test syrup measuring, soda preparation, mixing, ice, sip counts, passing, discarding, and effect cleanup.
7. Confirm all inventory items remain unique where metadata is required.
8. Publish documentation updates alongside the resource release.

## Support checklist

When reporting a problem, include the resource version, framework, inventory and version, relevant sanitized console errors, the exact action performed, and whether the issue occurs on a clean test configuration. Never share server keys or private player data.

title: G7 Black Market Phone
description: Install the G7 Black Market Phone burner-phone system and its optional integrations.
markdown:
# G7 Black Market Phone — Installation

A Samsung-style burner phone for ordering contraband. It includes synced drop vans and dealers, burner calls with face-to-face meets, a camera and gallery, global and private chat, stock, heat and police dispatch. It works on its own or together with **G7 Black Market**.

---

## Requirements

| Resource | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [oxmysql](https://github.com/overextended/oxmysql) | **Yes** | Database |
| OneSync | **Yes** | Legacy or Infinity. Drop vans and dealers are created by the server |
| A framework | **Yes** | **QBCore**, **Qbox** or **ESX** (detected automatically) |
| An inventory | **Yes** | **g7_inventory** (recommended), ox_inventory, qs-inventory, qb-inventory, ps-inventory, codem-inventory, core_inventory or your framework's built-in inventory |
| [screenshot-basic](https://github.com/citizenfx/screenshot-basic) | For the camera | Without it, the Camera and Gallery apps hide themselves |
| g7_blackmarket | Optional | Adds shared reputation, the Contracts app, market events on phone prices and weapon serials |
| ox_lib | Recommended | Notifications and progress bars |
| ox_target / qb-target | Optional | For collecting orders and talking to dealers. Without a target script, players get `[E]` prompts |
| A dispatch script | Optional | ps-dispatch, cd_dispatch, qs-dispatch, rcore_dispatch or core_dispatch (detected automatically). It falls back to a built-in police alert |

---

## 1. Add the resource

1. Download `g7_blackmarket_phone` from your Keymaster / Tebex account.
2. Extract it into your `resources` folder. Keep the folder name **`g7_blackmarket_phone`**.

---

## 2. server.cfg

```cfg
ensure oxmysql
ensure ox_lib
ensure qbx_core               # or qb-core / es_extended
ensure g7_inventory           # or your inventory
ensure screenshot-basic       # for the camera

ensure g7_blackmarket         # optional, start it BEFORE the phone
ensure g7_blackmarket_phone
```

---

## 3. Database

**Nothing to do.** All tables are created automatically on the first start:

`g7_bmp_profiles` · `g7_bmp_orders` · `g7_bmp_messages` · `g7_bmp_stock` · `g7_bmp_photos`

---

## 4. Items & images

Everything you need is in the **`install/`** folder. Use the file for your inventory and **skip any items you already have**.

| Inventory | Item file | Copy images from → to |
|---|---|---|
| **g7_inventory** | `install/ox_inventory_g7_inventory_qbox.lua` → `g7_inventory/data/items.lua` | `install/images/ox/` → `g7_inventory/web/images/` |
| **ox_inventory / Qbox** | `install/ox_inventory_g7_inventory_qbox.lua` → `ox_inventory/data/items.lua` | `install/images/ox/` → `ox_inventory/web/images/` |
| **QBCore** (qb / ps / lj / codem / core) | `install/qb-core_shared_items.lua` → `qb-core/shared/items.lua` | `install/images/qb/` → your inventory's image folder |
| **qs-inventory** | `install/qs-inventory_items.lua` → `qs-inventory/shared/items.lua` | `install/images/qb/` → `qs-inventory/html/images/` |
| **ESX** (default inventory) | Run `install/esx_items.sql` on your database | `install/images/qb/` → your inventory's image folder |

### The burner phone item

The phone item is **`blackmarket_phone`**. How it opens depends on your inventory:

- **g7_inventory / ox_inventory / Qbox:** the item entry in the install file already opens the phone:
  ```lua
  ['blackmarket_phone'] = { label = 'Burner Phone', weight = 200, stack = false, close = true,
      description = 'Untraceable. Order from the underground.',
      client = { image = 'blackmarket_phone.png', export = 'g7_blackmarket_phone.usePhone' } },
  ```
- **QBCore / ESX:** the script registers the item as usable automatically.
- **Any other inventory:** when the item is used, run `TriggerServerEvent('g7_blackmarket_phone:server:use')` on the client, or `exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:UsePhone(source)` on the server.

To open the phone with a command as well, set `Config.Phone.command = 'bmphone'`.

---

## 5. Permissions

```cfg
# ACE
add_ace group.admin g7bmphone.admin allow
```

Groups listed in `Config.Admin.groups` (`admin`, `god` and `superadmin` by default) also count as admins.

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/bmphoneadmin` | Admin | Opens the phone straight to the **Admin** app: overview, stock, players (heat and rep), orders (cancel or refund) and chat moderation |

---

## 6. Configure

Open `config.lua`. Settings to check first:

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Config.Phone.prop` | `prop_npc_phone_02` | Phone model in the player's hand. Stream your own prop and put its name here |
| `Config.Phone.ui` | Frost blue | Theme, brand, logo, position, wallpapers, frame colors and the size limits players can pick |
| `Config.Phone.ui.allowCustomize` | `true` | Lets players change wallpaper, frame color and phone size in Settings |
| `Config.PaymentAccount` | `'dirty'` | Account used to pay for orders |
| `Config.Catalog` | 16 items | Phone market stock, prices, rep locks and heat |
| `Config.Stock` | enabled | Limited stock and restocking |
| `Config.Heat` | enabled | Heat per order, how fast it cools down and the dispatch chance |
| `Config.Dispatch` | `'auto'` | Dispatch system, police jobs and minimum police online |
| `Config.Restrictions` | police / EMS, 3 zones | Blocked jobs and no-signal zones |
| `Config.Calls` | 3 dealers | Burner call dealers, their stock, rep requirements and cooldowns |
| `Config.Camera` | enabled | Photo quality, size limit and photos kept per player |
| `Config.DropLocations` | 35 locations | Drop van and meet spots |
| `Config.Logs` | `'none'` | `'discord'` (webhook) or `'fivemanage'` (API key) |

> **Test the drop locations on your map.** The 35 drop and meet spots use standard GTA streets and parking lots. If one clashes with an MLO, move it, or add `ped = vector4(...)` to place the dealer yourself.

---

## 7. Test it

1. Restart the server.
2. Give yourself a phone: `/additem [your id] blackmarket_phone 1` on g7_inventory or ox. On QB use `/giveitem`.
3. Use the phone. Order something from **Market** and wait for the driver.
4. Open **Phone → Contacts** and call **Dmitri** to set up a street meet.
5. Open **Camera**, press `Enter` to take a photo, then share it from **Gallery**.

---

## Exports

```lua
-- server
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:UsePhone(src)
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:GetHeat(src)
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:AddHeat(src, amount)   -- trusted resources only
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:GetStock(item)
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:SetStock(item, amount)

-- client
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:usePhone()             -- for inventory item exports
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:IsOpen()
exports.g7_blackmarket_phone:Close()
```

---

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Phone doesn't open | Make sure the item is set up (step 4) and the player isn't on a blocked job or in a no-signal zone |
| "You don't have a burner" | `Config.Phone.requireItem = true` checks for the item on every action. Give the player `blackmarket_phone` |
| Camera / Gallery missing | Start `screenshot-basic` before the phone |
| Photos fail to save | Lower `Config.Camera.quality` or raise `Config.Camera.maxBytes` |
| Dealer doesn't answer | Every dealer has a `noAnswerChance`. Set it to `0` while testing. Ghost needs 3,500 rep |
| Van or dealer doesn't appear | OneSync must be enabled. Check the server console for errors |
| Phone prop floats or clips | Adjust `Config.Phone.offset` and `Config.Phone.rotation` |
| Phone is too big or small | Players can change the size in **Settings → Phone size**, or set `Config.Phone.ui.scale` |

Need help? Join the **[G7 Development Discord](https://discord.gg/P6XQ4N6M95)**.

title: G7 Black Market
description: Install G7 Black Market contracts, crews, heists, laundering, and market events.
markdown:
# G7 Black Market — Installation

A contract, reputation and black market system with crews, heists, laundering, market events and weekly prizes. It works on its own or together with **G7 Black Market Phone**.

---

## Requirements

| Resource | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [oxmysql](https://github.com/overextended/oxmysql) | **Yes** | Database |
| A framework | **Yes** | **QBCore**, **Qbox** or **ESX** (detected automatically). Custom frameworks are supported, see [Custom framework](#custom-framework) |
| An inventory | **Yes** | **g7_inventory** (recommended), ox_inventory, qs-inventory, qb-inventory, ps-inventory, codem-inventory, core_inventory or your framework's built-in inventory |
| [ox_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib) | Recommended | Notifications, progress bars and the heist hacking minigame. Falls back to framework or native versions without it |
| ox_target / qb-target | Optional | Used for the mission givers. Without a target script, players get `[E]` prompts |
| A vehicle keys script | Optional | qbx_vehiclekeys, qb-vehiclekeys, Renewed-Vehiclekeys, wasabi_carlock or MrNewbVehicleKeys, for contract cars and purchased cars |

---

## 1. Add the resource

1. Download `g7_blackmarket` from your Keymaster / Tebex account.
2. Extract it into your `resources` folder. Keep the folder name **`g7_blackmarket`**.

---

## 2. server.cfg

Start it **after** your database, framework and inventory, and **before** `g7_blackmarket_phone` if you use the phone:

```cfg
ensure oxmysql
ensure ox_lib            # recommended
ensure qbx_core          # or qb-core / es_extended
ensure g7_inventory      # or your inventory
ensure ox_target         # optional

ensure g7_blackmarket
ensure g7_blackmarket_phone   # optional
```

---

## 3. Database

**Nothing to do.** All tables are created automatically on the first start:

`g7_blackmarket_players` · `g7_blackmarket_history` · `g7_blackmarket_crews` · `g7_blackmarket_crew_members` · `g7_blackmarket_launder` · `g7_blackmarket_serials` · `g7_blackmarket_pending`

---

## 4. Items & images

Everything you need is in the **`install/`** folder. Use the file for your inventory and **skip any items you already have**.

| Inventory | Item file | Copy images from → to |
|---|---|---|
| **g7_inventory** | `install/ox_inventory_g7_inventory_qbox.lua` → `g7_inventory/data/items.lua` | `install/images/ox/` → `g7_inventory/web/images/` |
| **ox_inventory / Qbox** | `install/ox_inventory_g7_inventory_qbox.lua` → `ox_inventory/data/items.lua` | `install/images/ox/` → `ox_inventory/web/images/` |
| **QBCore** (qb / ps / lj / codem / core) | `install/qb-core_shared_items.lua` → `qb-core/shared/items.lua` | `install/images/qb/` → your inventory's image folder |
| **qs-inventory** | `install/qs-inventory_items.lua` → `qs-inventory/shared/items.lua` | `install/images/qb/` → `qs-inventory/html/images/` |
| **ESX** (default inventory) | Run `install/esx_items.sql` on your database | `install/images/qb/` → your inventory's image folder |

> **Item names are translated automatically.** The config uses ox / g7 names (`WEAPON_PISTOL`, `ammo-9`, `armour`). On QB-style inventories the script switches them to the QB names (`weapon_pistol`, `pistol_ammo`, `armor`), so you don't need to edit the config. Add your own renames in `Config.ItemAliases`, for example `['black_money'] = 'markedbills'`.

> **Pictures always show.** Every image is also bundled in `html/images/`, so the market shows pictures even before you copy them into your inventory.

### Dirty money

| Setup | Dirty money is |
|---|---|
| g7_inventory or ox_inventory (any framework) | the `black_money` **item** |
| QBCore / Qbox with another inventory | the `black_money` **item** (change it in `Config.Accounts.dirty`) |
| ESX default inventory | the `black_money` **account** |

---

## 5. Permissions

Admin commands accept any of these:

```cfg
# ACE (any framework)
add_ace group.admin g7.admin allow
```

- QBCore `admin` / `god`
- ESX `admin` / `superadmin`

| Command | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/bmsetrep [id] [amount]` | Admin / console | Sets a player's reputation (this also sets their rank and tier) |
| `/bmevent sale\|crackdown\|rep\|rare` | Admin / console | Starts a market event right away |
| `/bmtrace [serial]` | Police jobs from `Config.Serials.policeJobs` | Traces a weapon serial. With no serial, it traces the weapon you're holding (ox / g7 only) |
| `/bmabandon` | Players | Abandons the active contract |

---

## 6. Configure

Open `config.lua`. Settings to check first:

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Config.Framework` | `'auto'` | `'qbox'`, `'qb'`, `'esx'` or `'custom'` |
| `Config.Inventory` | `'auto'` | Checks **g7_inventory** first |
| `Config.Target` | `'auto'` | `'ox_target'`, `'qb-target'` or `'none'` |
| `Config.Theme.preset` | `'frost'` | UI theme: `frost` (blue), `g7` (purple), `toxic`, `ember`, `gold`, `mono` or `custom`. Uses the same engine as the other G7 scripts |
| `Config.BlacklistedJobs` | police jobs | Jobs that can't use the black market |
| `Config.Givers` | 3 givers | Mission giver peds, blips and locations |
| `Config.Ranks` | 8 ranks | Rep needed for each rank and the tier it unlocks |
| `Config.Missions` | 12 contracts | Contracts, crew contracts and heists |
| `Config.ShopItems` | weapons, ammo, tools, contraband, vehicles | Market stock, prices and tiers |
| `Config.Crews` | enabled | Crew cost, size, rep share and levels |
| `Config.Laundering` | enabled | Rates, daily limits and seizure chance |
| `Config.MarketEvents` | enabled | Random sales, crackdowns, double rep and rare shipments |
| `Config.WeeklyPrizes` | Monday 18:00 | Weekly leaderboard prizes (server time) |
| `Config.Serials` | enabled | Weapon serials and police tracing |
| `Config.Logs` | disabled | Discord webhook logging |

> **Test the coordinates on your map.** Heist sites (`Config.HeistLocations`) and mission locations use standard GTA locations. If you run MLOs that cover any of them, move those spots.

---

## 7. Test it

1. Restart the server, or run `ensure g7_blackmarket`.
2. The console should show:
   ```
   [G7] g7_blackmarket framework: qbox
   [G7] g7_blackmarket inventory: g7_inventory
   ```
3. Go to **Vince** at the Terminal docks (blip on the map) and talk to him.
4. To unlock everything, run `/bmsetrep [your id] 18000` (Kingpin, tier 5).

---

## Custom framework

Set `Config.Framework = 'custom'` and fill in the `Custom` table at the top of `bridge/server.lua`. It takes identifier, name, job, money get/add/remove and admin check functions.

---

## Exports

```lua
-- server
exports.g7_blackmarket:GetReputation(src)
exports.g7_blackmarket:GetRank(src)                       -- { index, name, tier, progress, next, nextRep }
exports.g7_blackmarket:AddReputation(src, amount, reason) -- trusted resources only
exports.g7_blackmarket:OpenRemote(src, tab)               -- trusted resources only
exports.g7_blackmarket:GetCrew(src)                       -- { id, name, tag, rep } or nil
exports.g7_blackmarket:GetActiveEvent()
exports.g7_blackmarket:GetPriceModifier(item, category)
exports.g7_blackmarket:GiveTrackedItem(src, item, qty, source)
exports.g7_blackmarket:TraceSerial(serial)                -- for MDTs
```

Trusted resources are listed in `Config.RemoteOpenResources`.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Market pictures don't show | Copy the images (step 4), or check that `inventory:imagepath` points to your images |
| "Not enough money" with dirty money | Make sure the player has the `black_money` item (see Dirty money) |
| Contract car won't start | Make sure your keys script is running. `Config.MissionVehicles.giveKeys = true` gives keys on entry |
| Can't find a stash spot | Spots show as small blips. If one landed somewhere unreachable, `/bmabandon` and take the contract again |
| Crew contract says you need more members | Crew members must be online and within `Config.Crews.joinRange` (100 m) of you |
| Heist hack is just a progress bar | Install ox_lib for the skill-check minigame |
| Nobody gets paid weekly | Players need at least `Config.WeeklyPrizes.minRep` rep that week. Offline winners are paid the next time they open the menu |

Need help? Join the **[G7 Development Discord](https://discord.gg/P6XQ4N6M95)**.

title: G7 Drug Sales
description: Install G7 Drug Sales and its companion trap-phone resource.
markdown:
# G7 Drug Sales — Installation This guide takes you from download to selling on your server in about 10 minutes. Follow the steps in order. > **Need help?** Open a ticket in our [Discord](https://discord.gg/P6XQ4N6M95). Have your framework, inventory and any F8 / server console errors ready. --- ## Requirements | | Supported | |---|---| | **Framework** | Qbox, QBCore, ESX | | **Inventory** | g7_inventory, ox_inventory, qs-inventory, qb-inventory (also ps-inventory / lj-inventory) | | **Target** | ox_target, qb-target, or none (built-in 3D text) | | **Database** | oxmysql *(optional, saves rep and stats. Without it the script uses the server's built-in KVP storage)* | There is **no ox_lib dependency**. The script detects your framework, inventory and target system automatically. --- ## 1. Download & Extract Download **G7 Drug Sales** from your [Tebex / Cfx.re Portal](https://g7-development.tebex.io/) and extract it. You'll get two resources: ``` g7_drugsales/ ← the script g7_trapphone/ ← the custom trap phone model (streamed prop) ``` Drop **both** folders into your server's `resources` folder, for example `resources/[g7]/`. > ⚠️ Don't put `g7_trapphone` *inside* `g7_drugsales`. They are two separate resources and FiveM won't load one that's nested in another. --- ## 2. server.cfg Add both resources **after** your framework, inventory, target and oxmysql: ```cfg ensure oxmysql # optional ensure qb-core # or qbx_core / es_extended ensure ox_inventory # or g7_inventory / qs-inventory / qb-inventory ensure ox_target # or qb-target (optional) ensure g7_trapphone ensure g7_drugsales ``` > ⚠️ Load order matters. If `g7_drugsales` starts before your framework or inventory, auto-detection can't find them. --- ## 3. Add the Items All item definitions are in `g7_drugsales/install/items/`. Pick the file for **your inventory** and skip any items you already have. **Items used by the script:** | Item name | Label | Used for | |---|---|---| | `trapphone` | Trap Phone | Opens the trap phone (usable) | | `black_money` | Dirty Money | Default payout item | | `weed_og-kush` | OG Kush | Drug | | `weed_white-widow` | White Widow | Drug | | `weed_purple-haze` | Purple Haze | Drug | | `cokebaggy` | Coke Baggy | Drug | | `crack_baggy` | Crack Baggy | Drug | | `xtcbaggy` | Ecstasy | Drug | | `meth` | Meth | Drug | | `oxy` | Oxy | Drug | | `lean` | Lean | Drug | ### g7_inventory / ox_inventory / Qbox File: `install/items/g7_inventory.lua` or `install/items/ox_inventory.lua` For ox_inventory, paste into `ox_inventory/data/items.lua`, inside the `return { }` table: ```lua ['trapphone'] = { label = 'Trap Phone', weight = 200, stack = false, close = true, description = 'Burner for the plug.', client = { export = 'g7_drugsales.useTrapPhone' }, }, ['black_money'] = { label = 'Dirty Money', weight = 0, stack = true, close = true }, ['weed_og-kush'] = { label = 'OG Kush', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['weed_white-widow'] = { label = 'White Widow', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['weed_purple-haze'] = { label = 'Purple Haze', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['cokebaggy'] = { label = 'Coke Baggy', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['crack_baggy'] = { label = 'Crack Baggy', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['xtcbaggy'] = { label = 'Ecstasy', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['meth'] = { label = 'Meth', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['oxy'] = { label = 'Oxy', weight = 50, stack = true, close = true }, ['lean'] = { label = 'Lean', weight = 250, stack = true, close = true }, ``` ### QBCore (qb-inventory / ps-inventory / lj-inventory) File: `install/items/qb_qbox_items.lua`. Paste it into `qb-core/shared/items.lua`, inside `QBShared.Items = { }`. ```lua ['trapphone'] = { name = 'trapphone', label = 'Trap Phone', weight = 200, type = 'item', image = 'trapphone.png', unique = true, useable = true, shouldClose = true, description = 'Burner for the plug.' }, -- ...the rest of the items are in the file ``` ### qs-inventory File: `install/items/qs_inventory.lua`. Paste it into `qs-inventory/shared/items.lua`, inside `ItemList = { }`. ### ESX (default inventory) Run `install/items/esx_items.sql` on your database. > ℹ️ On ESX, `black_money` is an **account**, not an item. See [Step 6](#6-payout-setup). --- ## 4. Add the Item Images All item images are in `g7_drugsales/install/images/`. They are 512×512 transparent PNGs, and each file is already named after its item. Copy **every `.png`** into your inventory's image folder: | Inventory | Image folder | |---|---| | g7_inventory | `g7_inventory/html/images/` | | ox_inventory | `ox_inventory/web/images/` | | qs-inventory | `qs-inventory/html/images/` | | qb-inventory | `qb-inventory/html/images/` | | ps-inventory / lj-inventory | `/html/images/` | The trap phone UI loads its drug images from the same folder, so this step covers both. --- ## 5. Database (optional) If **oxmysql** is running, the script creates its `g7_drugsales` table automatically on first start. You don't need to run anything. If you'd rather create it yourself, run `install/g7_drugsales.sql`. Without oxmysql, rep and stats are saved in the server's built-in KVP storage, and no SQL is needed. --- ## 6. Payout Setup By default, players are paid with the `black_money` **item**. Change this in `config.lua` to match your server: ```lua Config.Payout = { Type = 'item', -- 'item' | 'account' | 'markedbills' Item = 'black_money', -- used when Type = 'item' Account = 'cash', -- used when Type = 'account' } ``` | Your setup | Use | |---|---| | g7_inventory / ox_inventory / qs-inventory | `Type = 'item'`, `Item = 'black_money'` | | ESX (default inventory) | `Type = 'account'`, `Account = 'black_money'` | | QBCore with marked bills | `Type = 'markedbills'` | | Clean cash | `Type = 'account'`, `Account = 'cash'` | --- ## 7. Trap Phone Model `g7_trapphone` already includes the G7 trap phone model, so there's nothing to configure. When a player opens the phone, it appears in their hand. If the model ever fails to load, the script falls back to the normal GTA phone automatically. **Adjusting how it sits in the hand** (admins): 1. Open the phone with `/drugphone`. 2. Run `/phoneprop x y z rx ry rz` (for example `/phoneprop 0.0 0.02 -0.01 0 0 180`). 3. Repeat until it looks right. Each run shows the line and copies it for you. 4. Paste it into `config.lua` → `Config.Phone.Prop` and restart the resource. --- ## 8. Admin Permissions The admin commands (`/g7dscoords`, `/phoneprop`) work for anyone with your framework's admin permission. To allow them with ACE permissions instead, add this to `server.cfg`: ```cfg add_ace group.admin g7drugsales.admin allow ``` --- ## 9. Restart & Test Restart your server, or run `ensure g7_trapphone` then `ensure g7_drugsales`. The server console should show: ``` [G7] g7_drugsales framework: qb inventory: ox_inventory [G7] g7_drugsales storage: oxmysql ``` **Quick test:** 1. Give yourself some product, e.g. `/giveitem 1 weed_og-kush 20` (QB) or `/additem 1 weed_og-kush 20` (ox). 2. Run `/selldrugs`, pick the drug, and wait for a customer to walk up. 3. Run `/drugphone` and accept an order in **Orders**. --- ## Commands | Command | Who | What it does | |---|---|---| | `/drugphone` | Everyone | Opens / closes the trap phone | | `/selldrugs` | Everyone | Starts corner selling (run it again to stop) | | `/stopselling` | Everyone | Stops corner selling | | `/canceldelivery` | Everyone | Cancels the active order or batch | | `/g7dscoords` | Admin | Copies a `vec4(...)` of your position for adding drop locations | | `/phoneprop x y z rx ry rz` | Admin | Positions the phone model in hand live | All command names can be changed in `Config.Commands`. To give the phone a keybind, set `Config.Keybinds.Phone` (for example `'F6'`). --- ## Adding Your Own Drugs Add an entry to `Config.Drugs`, using the **item name** as the key: ```lua ['my_drug'] = { label = 'My Drug', street = { price = { 100, 180 }, amount = { 1, 3 } }, -- corner selling delivery = { price = { 140, 220 }, amount = { 4, 12 } }, -- phone orders batch = { price = { 90, 150 }, amount = { 15, 45 } }, -- gang batch drops minLevel = 1, -- rep level needed (optional) }, ``` Other resources can also register drugs from their own server code: ```lua exports.g7_drugsales:RegisterDrug('lean_cup', { label = 'Lean Cup', street = { price = { 350, 500 }, amount = { 1, 2 } }, delivery = { price = { 420, 560 }, amount = { 2, 8 } }, batch = { price = { 300, 420 }, amount = { 8, 30 } }, }) ``` --- ## Overriding Auto-Detection Auto-detection works for most servers. To force a specific system, set it in `config.lua`: ```lua Config.Framework = 'auto' -- 'qbx' | 'qb' | 'esx' Config.Inventory = 'auto' -- 'g7_inventory' | 'ox_inventory' | 'qs-inventory' | 'qb-inventory' Config.Target = 'auto' -- 'ox_target' | 'qb-target' | '3dtext' Config.Storage = 'auto' -- 'oxmysql' | 'kvp' ``` --- ## Troubleshooting
Console says "framework: standalone" or the wrong inventory `g7_drugsales` is starting before your framework or inventory. Move `ensure g7_drugsales` lower in `server.cfg`, or set `Config.Framework` / `Config.Inventory` by hand.
"You have nothing to sell" The item names in your inventory must match the keys in `Config.Drugs` exactly, including dashes and underscores (e.g. `weed_og-kush`). Also check the drug's `minLevel`.
Drug images don't show in the phone or the sell menu Copy the PNGs from `install/images/` into your inventory's image folder ([Step 4](#4-add-the-item-images)). If your inventory keeps images somewhere else, change the path in `Config.ImagePaths`.
No "Sell drugs" option on customers Make sure your target resource starts **before** `g7_drugsales`. For customers in cars, aim at the **car**, not the driver. To skip target completely, set `Config.Target = '3dtext'`.
Players don't get paid The payout item or account doesn't exist on your server. See [Step 6](#6-payout-setup). ESX servers using the default inventory need `Type = 'account'`.
The phone is a normal GTA phone, not the G7 model `g7_trapphone` isn't running, or it starts after `g7_drugsales`. Make sure `ensure g7_trapphone` comes first and the console shows no stream errors.
No customers spawn / "Too hot around here" You're inside a blacklisted zone (PD, hospital). Move away, or edit `Config.Zones.Blacklisted`. If `Config.Zones.RestrictToZones = true`, you can only sell inside a hotspot.
"Nobody is buying right now..." There aren't enough police on duty for `Config.Police.MinCops`. Set the values to `0` to disable the requirement.
--- **G7 Development** · [Store](https://g7-development.tebex.io/) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/P6XQ4N6M95)

title: G7 Inventory
description: Install G7 Inventory and migrate from an existing inventory system.
markdown:
# G7 Inventory — Installation

G7 Inventory is a drop-in replacement for **ox_inventory**. Scripts that use `exports.ox_inventory`, listen to `ox_inventory:*` events or check whether `ox_inventory` is started keep working without changes. Your framework is detected automatically.

**Supported frameworks:** Qbox · ESX Legacy · QBCore · ox_core · ND_Core · Standalone

---

## Requirements

| Resource | Notes |
|---|---|
| [ox_lib](https://github.com/overextended/ox_lib) | Latest release |
| [oxmysql](https://github.com/overextended/oxmysql) | Latest release |
| OneSync | Legacy or Infinity |
| [ox_target](https://github.com/overextended/ox_target) | Optional, only if you want target interactions |

---

## 1. Remove your old inventory

G7 Inventory registers itself as `ox_inventory`, so **it can't run alongside another inventory**.

- **From ox_inventory:** stop it and remove it from your server (or move it out of your resources folder). Your existing items, stashes, trunks and gloveboxes are kept. G7 uses the same database layout, so nothing needs converting.
- **From qb-inventory, ps-inventory or lj-inventory:** remove the inventory resource, then follow [Moving over from another inventory](#5-moving-over-from-another-inventory) after the first start.
- **From the default ESX inventory:** nothing to remove. Follow [Moving over from another inventory](#5-moving-over-from-another-inventory) after the first start.

> **Back up your database before installing.** Any inventory change is worth a backup first.

---

## 2. Add the resource

1. Download `g7_inventory` and extract it into your resources folder.
2. Keep the folder name **`g7_inventory`**. It's used for image paths and exports.

```
resources/
└── [inventory]/
    └── g7_inventory/
        ├── client/
        ├── data/
        ├── locales/
        ├── server/
        ├── shared/
        ├── sql/
        ├── web/
        ├── config.lua
        └── fxmanifest.lua
```

---

## 3. Update server.cfg

Start G7 Inventory **after** oxmysql, ox_lib and your framework, and **before** any script that uses the inventory.

```cfg
ensure oxmysql
ensure ox_lib
ensure qbx_core          # or es_extended / qb-core / ox_core / ND_Core
ensure g7_inventory

# everything that uses the inventory goes below
ensure ox_target
ensure [jobs]
ensure [scripts]
```

> **Remove this line if you have it.** Most servers that ran ox_inventory have:
> ```cfg
> setr inventory:imagepath "nui://ox_inventory/web/images"
> ```
> G7 redirects it automatically, but it's cleaner to delete it or point it at G7:
> ```cfg
> setr inventory:imagepath "nui://g7_inventory/web/images"
> ```

---

## 4. Start the server

On first start, G7 creates the tables and columns it needs:

| Table / column | Used for |
|---|---|
| `inventory` column on your framework's player table | Player inventories |
| `ox_inventory` | Stashes |
| `glovebox` / `trunk` columns on your framework's vehicle table | Vehicle storage |
| `g7_progression` | Levels, XP, skills and daily missions |
| `g7_players` | Player inventories, **standalone servers only** |

If your database user can't create tables, run `sql/install.sql` by hand instead.

When everything is working, the server console shows:

```
[g7_inventory] ready - framework: qbx, 507 items, ox_inventory API v2.48 compatible
```

Check that the framework named there is the one you use. To force a different one, see [Framework setup](#framework-setup).

---

## 5. Moving over from another inventory

Skip this step if you came from **ox_inventory**: your data already works.

Player inventories in the old qb-inventory and ESX formats are **converted automatically** the first time each player joins. The commands below convert everything at once, and they're **required** for qb-inventory stashes and ESX weapon loadouts.

Run the matching command **once**, from the **server console** (txAdmin live console or the server window, not in game), while no players are online:

| Coming from | Command | What it converts |
|---|---|---|
| qb-inventory / ps / lj | `g7convert qb` | All player inventories (`amount` / `info` format) |
| qb-inventory / ps / lj | `g7convert qbstashes` | Stashes, trunks and gloveboxes (**required**) |
| ESX (default inventory) | `g7convert esx` | Player inventories and weapon loadouts (**required** for loadouts) |

Wait for the console to print `conversion finished - restart the server`, then restart.

### Item lists

G7 reads items from `data/items.lua` and weapons from `data/weapons.lua`, both in **ox_inventory format**. You can paste an existing ox `items.lua` straight in.

QBCore and ESX servers can also keep their framework item lists. With this setting on, items from `QBCore.Shared.Items` or the ESX `items` table that aren't in `data/items.lua` are added automatically:

```lua
-- config.lua
Config.ImportFrameworkItems = true
```

> **Items that don't exist are never deleted.** If a player has an item that isn't in your item list, it stays saved and the console shows `unknown item "name" ... kept in storage`. Add the item to `data/items.lua` and it appears again for the player.

---

## Framework setup

The framework is detected in this order: **Qbox → ESX → QBCore → ox_core → ND_Core → Standalone**.

To force one, set it in `server.cfg`:

```cfg
setr inventory:framework "qbx"     # qbx | esx | qb | ox | nd | standalone
```

### Qbox
Works out of the box. Money is kept in sync with Qbox's cash account.

> Don't add `provide 'qb-inventory'` on Qbox. Qbox refuses to save players while it thinks qb-inventory is running.

### ESX Legacy
Works out of the box. G7 uses ESX's built-in ox_inventory support, so nothing needs changing in ESX. `money` and `black_money` are handled as account items.

### QBCore
Works out of the box. QBCore item functions (`Player.Functions.AddItem`, `RemoveItem`, `HasItem`…) and the `qb-inventory`, `ps-inventory` and `lj-inventory` exports are bridged to G7.

If a script refuses to work because it checks whether `qb-inventory` is **started**, open `fxmanifest.lua` and uncomment:

```lua
-- provide 'qb-inventory'
```

**QBCore only.** Never do this on Qbox.

### ox_core / ND_Core
Supported through their existing ox_inventory integration. No extra steps.

### Standalone
Players are identified by their FiveM license and stored in the `g7_players` table. Permission groups come from ACE:

```cfg
add_ace group.admin g7.group.admin allow
add_ace group.police g7.group.police allow
```

---

## Item images

Item images go in `web/images/` as **`<item name>.png`**, for example `water.png` or `WEAPON_PISTOL.png`.

- Use lowercase `.png` extensions. Linux servers treat `.PNG` and `.png` as different files.
- An item can use a different image with `client = { image = 'other_name.png' }` in its definition.
- To host images on a website instead:
  ```cfg
  setr inventory:imagepath "https://cdn.example.com/items"
  ```
  If an image can't be loaded from there, G7 falls back to its own `web/images` folder.

---

## Keybinds

| Default key | Action |
|---|---|
| `F2` | Open inventory (also opens a nearby drop, or the trunk when you're behind an unlocked vehicle) |
| `K` | Open trunk, glovebox, dumpster or stash |
| `TAB` | Show the hotbar |
| `1` – `5` | Use fast slots |
| `Z` (hold) | Quick wheel |
| `R` | Reload |

Players can rebind these in **Settings → Key Bindings → FiveM**. To change the defaults for everyone:

```cfg
setr inventory:keys ["F2", "K", "TAB"]    # inventory, secondary, hotbar
```

---

## Common server.cfg options

All ox_inventory `inventory:*` convars work. The most used ones:

```cfg
setr inventory:slots 50               # player slots
setr inventory:weight 30000           # player max weight, in grams
setr inventory:target false           # true = use ox_target for stashes, shops, benches
setr inventory:police ["police", "sheriff"]
setr inventory:screenblur true
setr inventory:weaponanims true
setr inventory:droplifetime 15        # minutes before dropped bags disappear (0 = never)
set  inventory:webhook "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/..."   # logs
set  inventory:loglevel 1             # 0 off, 1 important, 2 everything
```

### Player card photos (optional)

The player card can show a Discord or Steam profile picture. Put the keys in `server.cfg` with **`set`**, never `setr` (which would send them to every player) and never in a Lua file:

```cfg
set g7:discordToken "your-bot-token"
set g7:steamApiKey  "your-steam-web-api-key"
```

---

## Configuration

Everything else lives in **`config.lua`**: themes, features, shops, drops, backpacks, weapons on back, encumbrance, progression and more. Any feature can be switched off under `Config.Features`.

Data files in `data/` use the same format as ox_inventory:

| File | Contains |
|---|---|
| `items.lua` | Items |
| `weapons.lua` | Weapons, attachments, tints and ammo |
| `shops.lua` | Shops and vending machines |
| `stashes.lua` | Stashes and lockers |
| `crafting.lua` | Crafting benches and recipes |
| `evidence.lua` | Police evidence lockers |
| `licenses.lua` | Purchasable licences |
| `vehicles.lua` | Trunk and glovebox sizes |
| `animations.lua` | Item use animations |
| `skills.lua` / `missions.lua` | Progression skills and daily missions |

Pasted ox data files that use ox's `shared` table (for example `groups = shared.police`) work without editing.

---

## Check your installation

1. Join the server and press **F2**. Your inventory opens with your items.
2. Run `/giveitem <your id> water 5` and check the water appears.
3. Drop an item, then press **F2** next to the bag to pick it up.
4. Open a vehicle trunk with **K** while standing behind it.
5. Run `/saveinv`. The console prints `saved N inventories`.

### Admin commands

Admin commands need `group.admin`. `/trade` is for every player, and `/clearevidence` is for police bosses.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/giveitem [id] [item] [count]` | Give an item (`/additem` works too) |
| `/removeitem [id] [item] [count]` | Remove an item |
| `/setitem [id] [item] [count]` | Set the exact amount of an item |
| `/viewinv [id]` | Look at a player's inventory |
| `/clearinv [id]` | Wipe a player's inventory |
| `/takeinv [id]` | Confiscate a player's inventory |
| `/restoreinv [id]` | Give a confiscated inventory back |
| `/saveinv` | Save all inventories now |
| `/addxp [id] [amount]` | Give progression XP |
| `/g7items` | Show how many items are loaded |
| `/trade [id]` | Ask a nearby player to trade (all players) |
| `/clearevidence [locker]` | Empty an evidence locker (police bosses) |

---

## Troubleshooting

**Images are missing or faded**
Check `server.cfg` for an `inventory:imagepath` line pointing at another resource, and remove it. Make sure each image is named exactly like the item, with a lowercase `.png` extension.

**`attempt to index a nil value (global 'shared')` on startup**
You're running a version older than 1.1.0. Update G7 Inventory.

**The console shows a different framework than yours**
Make sure your framework starts **before** `g7_inventory` in `server.cfg`, or force it with `setr inventory:framework`.

**`could not read inventory of ...` in the console**
G7 couldn't reach your database when the player joined. It retries 3 times. If that fails, the inventory stays read-only for that session so nothing gets overwritten. Check that oxmysql is connected, then ask the player to reconnect.

**A QBCore script says the inventory isn't started**
Uncomment `provide 'qb-inventory'` in `fxmanifest.lua` (QBCore only).

**Another inventory is still running**
Only one inventory can run. Remove ox_inventory, qb-inventory, ps-inventory or lj-inventory from your resources and `server.cfg`.

---

## Updating

1. Back up `config.lua` and anything you changed in `data/`.
2. Replace the whole `g7_inventory` folder, so the built UI files in `web/build` are replaced too.
3. Put your `config.lua` and `data/` files back, then compare them with the new versions for any new settings. The changelog lists them.
4. Restart the server.
